evidence.supportingExcerpt: A full set has three parts. Spirometry has the person breathe in fully and blow out as hard and as long as possible, measuring the forced vital capacity (FVC) and how fast air leaves; the forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) and its ratio to FVC are the usual numbers. The ATS/ERS 2019 spirometry standard describes the test as the maximal volume of air a person can inspire and expire with maximal effort, reports FEV1/FVC as a decimal fraction, and sets acceptability and repeatability criteria for each manoeuvre, so a poor-effort test is a quality problem before it is a finding. Spirometry is used to look for obstructive conditions, in which the airways narrow so air flows out with difficulty, as in asthma, bronchitis and emphysema (MedlinePlus). A lung volume test, often done by body plethysmography in a sealed booth, measures the total lung capacity (TLC), the amount of air the lungs can hold; restrictive conditions, in which the lungs cannot fill fully, such as pulmonary fibrosis and interstitial lung disease, lower it. The diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) has the person breathe in a gas mixture with a trace of carbon monoxide and a tracer gas, hold the breath for about 10 seconds and breathe out; it shows how well gas crosses into the blood. The ERS/ATS 2022 interpretation standard explains that a low DLCO with normal alveolar volume can be consistent with pulmonary vascular impairment, emphysema with preserved volume or anaemia. Low alveolar volume with low or normal transfer coefficient can accompany interstitial lung disease or emphysema with loss of lung volume. These are patterns to interpret, not diagnoses from one value. The 2017 ERS/ATS standard asks for no smoking or other carbon-monoxide exposure on the day of the test, recording the last cigarette and accounting for recent or heavy exposure. Its preparation instructions are technical test conditions, not an individual treatment plan.

points.requirement: Three roles: baseline, one input to diagnosis (Conte 2022 panel: spirometry and DLCO with history, saturation, infection labs, CT), follow-up; low DLCO usual in interstitial disease, often with restriction.

evidence.explanation: Baseline, diagnostic input and follow-up are distinct; normal spirometry or low DLCO cannot diagnose or exclude all interstitial injury, and the product label does not mandate scheduled PFTs.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Their place in drug-related lung injury. A baseline records a person's own starting point, which makes a later change easier to read than a comparison with a population average. In diagnosis the tests are one input: an Italian multidisciplinary expert-opinion panel on drug-induced interstitial lung disease lists spirometry and DLCO among the diagnostic components alongside history, vital signs including oxygen saturation, laboratory and microbial tests to exclude infection, and computed tomography, stratifies management by CTCAE grade, and notes that there were no specific guidelines at the time (Conte et al., 2022). In follow-up, repeat testing can show whether function is recovering or worsening. They do not replace imaging: the trastuzumab deruxtecan label asks for symptom monitoring and radiographic evaluation of suspected interstitial lung disease, and neither it nor the datopotamab deruxtecan label mentions scheduled breathing tests. For scale, adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in 12.1 per cent of patients given trastuzumab deruxtecan in DESTINY-Breast04, 0.8 per cent grade 5 (Modi et al., 2022), and a prior lung event can bear on eligibility for later treatment. A test pattern does not identify cause, since many conditions lower DLCO; that normal spirometry does not rule out interstitial disease is an evidence-reading distinction between airflow and gas transfer; the 2022 standard also states that a result within the reference range does not exclude disease.

evidence.explanation: Baseline, diagnostic input and follow-up are distinct; normal spirometry or low DLCO cannot diagnose or exclude all interstitial injury, and the product label does not mandate scheduled PFTs.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional example, a person receiving an antibody-drug conjugate develops a dry cough, normal spirometry, a lower DLCO than baseline and a lower haemoglobin. The gas-transfer result needs haemoglobin-aware interpretation: it is not by itself a diagnosis of pneumonitis. Normal airflow measurements do not establish normal gas transfer. Clinical assessment combines history, symptoms, imaging and other appropriate tests; the trastuzumab deruxtecan label specifically calls for radiographic evaluation of suspected disease. Neither a low DLCO nor an arbitrary change threshold supplies a monitoring or treatment rule for every product. A reduced DLCO can accompany anaemia, emphysema, pulmonary vascular disease or interstitial injury; a test pattern alone does not select among causes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

points.requirement: Describe lymphodepletion as part of the full regimen, including its effects on competing cells, blood counts and infection risk; do not attribute all harm to the engineered cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Why preparing the body can help transferred cells, and what it costs. In mouse adoptive-transfer experiments, a nonmyeloablative regimen enhanced antitumour effect even without regulatory T cells, through greater function of tumour-reactive CD8-positive T cells rather than greater numbers; interleukin-7 and interleukin-15 were required, and removing endogenous cells that respond to those cytokines reproduced the effect, which points to lymphodepletion removing cells that act as cytokine sinks (Gattinoni et al.). That is a mouse mechanism and it does not describe an empty physical space. When a trial tests conditioning, transferred cells and cytokine support together, the outcomes belong to the whole package: in the phase 3 tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte trial in advanced melanoma (Rohaan et al.; 168 patients, 86 per cent with disease refractory to anti-PD-1 treatment), cells were infused after nonmyeloablative cyclophosphamide plus fludarabine and followed by high-dose interleukin-2, and grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in all patients given TILs, mainly chemotherapy-related myelosuppression. Nonmyeloablative therefore does not mean harmless.

points.requirement: Distinguish instruction delivery to unintended cells from harmful recognition of an intended antigen on healthy tissue.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.
evidence.explanation: Recipient-cell delivery and recognition of the intended antigen on healthy tissue are different steps and hazards. points.requirement: Keep Morgan's fatal-toxicity report tied to its particular receptor, dose and regimen, and its proposed normal-lung mechanism as the authors' hypothesis, not a universal risk rate.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Two primary reports show the contrast. A patient with colon cancer metastatic to the lungs and liver received 10 billion autologous T cells expressing a trastuzumab-based CAR against ERBB2 (HER2), the largest number permitted in the first dose-escalation cohort, the day after a lymphodepleting regimen of cyclophosphamide (60 mg/kg daily for 2 days) and fludarabine (25 mg/m2 for 5 days). Within 15 minutes the patient had respiratory distress, chest imaging showed pulmonary oedema, and the patient died 5 days after treatment, with marked rises in interferon-gamma, GM-CSF, tumour necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-6 and interleukin-10. At autopsy multiple organs showed systemic ischaemia and haemorrhagic microangiopathic injury and the lungs diffuse alveolar damage; histological examination of autopsy tissue found ERBB2 at 3+ in liver metastases and 2+ in lung metastases and much lower levels in normal lung parenchyma, normal liver and normal breast. The authors hypothesised that highly active ERBB2-directed T cells recognised ERBB2 on normal lung cells on first pass through the lung and released inflammatory cytokines that began a cascade ending in multiorgan failure; the autopsy findings were read as initial lung injury followed by days of hypotension and ischaemia, and the authors call the significance of the cells' reactivity against cultured primary cells unclear. This is a single case, with a stated dose and conditioning, whose mechanism is the authors' hypothesis and which gives no incidence for any CAR product (Morgan et al., 2010). In a trial of an affinity-enhanced T-cell receptor against HLA-A*01-restricted MAGE-A3 in myeloma and melanoma, the first two patients developed cardiogenic shock and died within days; no MAGE-A3 expression was detected in heart tissue at autopsy, and beating cardiomyocytes made from induced pluripotent stem cells triggered T-cell killing through recognition of an unrelated peptide from titin. That is off-target recognition of an unintended molecule, not the intended target in the wrong tissue (Linette et al., 2013).

evidence.supportingExcerpt: How the question is asked before and during trials. FDA's CAR T-cell development guidance says to assess both undesired targeting of healthy tissue that expresses the intended antigen (on-target/off-tumour) and unintended targeting of other antigens, using examples such as tissue cross-reactivity studies with an antibody carrying the same recognition domain, protein arrays, cytotoxicity and cytokine-release testing on panels of primary cells, cell lines or stem-cell-derived organ systems, and relevant animal models, and encourages a combination of methods; antigen recognition domains can differ in affinity or avidity or recognise a different site, which should be evaluated, and CAR T cells can carry added components such as suicide genes. In practice a readout is a staining intensity or positive fraction, a binding profile, killing or cytokine release by healthy cells at a named time, and finally organ injury in the treated population; stained fixed tissue does not show a living organ's accessibility, an animal model may lack the human target, and a negative result in one panel is not a safety certificate. No universal expression cut-off is given here because no source read gives one. Whether affinity tuning, recognition logic or control switches improve safety for a particular design needs that design's own evidence. The 2026 ASTCT consensus abstract lists on-target, off-tumour toxicity among the toxicities for which it considered definitions and grading; its criteria were not readable.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A receptor-bearing cell, its genetic instructions and its receptor protein are different objects. For a protein-coding instruction, DNA is transcribed into RNA, and a ribosome translates usable messenger RNA into protein. Delivered messenger RNA starts at the translation step. Folding and transport to the membrane still have to occur before a surface receptor can bind its target. In this schematic sequence, simplified shapes and an arrow from recognition toward a response do not show that every cell expressed the receptor or completed killing.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Three design labels are easy to confuse. Replication-defective means the delivered particle lacks the machinery to propagate as an ordinary virus, which does not replace testing: FDA guidance sets out testing of retroviral vector products, lentiviral ones included, for replication-competent virus during manufacture and in patient follow-up. Self-inactivating means regulatory sequences in the long terminal repeats are disabled: in the original design a 133 base-pair deletion in the U3 region of the 3' repeat was copied to the 5' repeat after reverse transcription and integration, and the vector still expressed from an internal promoter in rat brain and eye (Miyoshi and colleagues). It does not mean the cassette cannot integrate. Integration-deficient means integrase is mutated: with a class 1 integrase mutation, residual integration was lower than with intact integrase by a factor of 500 to 1,250, expression was transient in dividing cell lines and long-lived in non-dividing neural cultures and in mouse brain, consistent with an episomal genome (Philippe and colleagues). The name does not promise zero integration or lasting expression in dividing cells such as T cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Where the DNA sits was measured in different systems. In sequential muscle biopsies taken 3 and 12 months after an intramuscular AAV vector expressing alpha-1 antitrypsin, most vector DNA was double-stranded circular episomes, and clones recovered from the biopsies were transcriptionally active (Schnepp and colleagues; abstract read, full text not retrievable). evidence.supportingExcerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

review.rationale: All ten later chapters and the guide index were read in full before owner-field inspection. Two original/later pairs are wholly byte-identical; the other originals were reconciled by complete diffs, including relocated paths, the index teaching changes and the later context section. Both 128/129-section inventories remain separate. The frozen inventory has 289 original and 291 later obligations, 294 distinct units and 65 non-credit version sections. One personal-context section retains its signature but receives no credit or copied details. Forty connected paragraphs, existing bounded root fields, four frozen PR-373 binder owners and the new MUC1 target carry the teaching. Three Frank detailed-source units and the Pfeiffer CD8-negative parent-gate qualifier remain uncredited. Thirty-six complete raw abstracts and 73 targeted whole passages across 14 papers retain their actual depth; no whole-paper read is claimed. Eight PNGs and both themes of three distinct Mermaid diagrams were freshly viewed. Fifty-two registered draft-root readers and four explicitly overlaid frozen peer readers, exact field/Markdown/API checks and summary loaders were verified. Earlier source assessments and unreviewed retained catalogue assertions are separately labelled; no main/live or named review credit is claimed.

points.requirement: Preserve separate tissue entry, target recognition, useful function and healthy-tissue safety barriers; improving one link or increasing cells does not establish the complete treatment chain.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rise in engineered cells in blood with few found in two tumour biopsies leaves distribution and infiltration unresolved. Blood abundance is not entry into a mass of tissue, and a biopsy represents its sampled place and time. If a receptor works in a simple culture but killing falls in a more complex model with the target still present, investigate access, cell state and the model’s other features with controlled perturbations. The contrast alone does not identify a macrophage, vessel or signalling pathway as the cause, or show that more expansion will solve it. Expression of PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3 or TIGIT, or a count of macrophages or suppressor cells, does not by itself establish which input caused the functional difference. Trafficking toward a site and infiltration into tissue are different steps, and vessel number does not measure perfusion. Chronic stimulation, low oxygen, limited nutrients and inhibitory signals are different hypotheses; exhaustion describes cell states rather than physical tiredness.
evidence.explanation: Entry, recognition, useful function and healthy-tissue harm are separate links; more cells do not establish a complete treatment chain. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A cell-therapy recognition claim needs the actual binder and accessible epitope, including tumour cells that lack it and relevant healthy cells. Sun’s TROP2 CAR used a sacituzumab-derived binding fragment. Human-cell and TNBC xenograft experiments tested antitumour activity; a separate murine-cell construct in mice expressing human TROP2 tested toxicity. The ungated construct caused lung injury and inflammation in that model. evidence.supportingExcerpt: How the question is asked before and during trials. Whether affinity tuning, recognition logic or control switches improve safety for a particular design needs that design's own evidence. The 2026 ASTCT consensus abstract lists on-target, off-tumour toxicity among the toxicities for which it considered definitions and grading; its criteria were not readable.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

Cytokine release syndrome can follow activation by engineered immune cells or T-cell-engaging treatments. Signals from several cell types can contribute to fever, hypotension, hypoxia and other organ effects. Infection or other conditions can produce similar findings or coexist with the syndrome.

The 2019 ASTCT consensus defines and grades CRS using attributed clinical findings, including fever at onset and the blood-pressure or oxygen support required. Its scale is a reporting framework, not a management algorithm. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

points.requirement: For inflammatory toxicity, retain onset, grade, affected organs and observation time as distinct outcomes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading CRS without over-reading a cytokine level. CRS is a clinical syndrome, graded from attributed findings and not from a cytokine concentration. In a mouse model of CD19 CAR T-cell CRS, severity was mediated not by CAR T-cell-derived cytokines but by IL-6, IL-1 and nitric oxide from the recipient's macrophages, and IL-1 blockade abated it (Giavridis et al.); that supports a multicell amplification mechanism and does not show the same sources or shares in every human product. Infection and other conditions can cause or accompany the same findings, so the cause of a fever cannot be read from timing alone. A comparable report gives its grading version, observation window and treated denominator, with onset, maximum grade, interventions and resolution. Safety belongs to the product, disease, tumour burden and preparation, so experience with one blood-cancer product does not supply a solid-tumour product's rate, and no severe CRS in a small early study does not rule out uncommon events. CRS is a different problem from injury to healthy tissue that carries the target (on-target, off-tumour) and from neurotoxicity (ICANS). The treatment need not carry a cytokine payload to trigger endogenous inflammatory signalling. Tumour response does not establish acceptable inflammatory risk, and mild CRS does not establish lack of anticancer activity. Stopping a treatment input does not guarantee immediate removal of released signals or established injury. In a fictional early study, no severe CRS and a modest cytokine rise would not make every fever harmless CRS: attribution, clinical findings, a named grading framework, treated denominator and observation window are still needed.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Among the 32 treated participants, 25 had cytokine release syndrome: 17 grade 1 or 2, six grade 3 and two grade 4. One person had brief, self-limited ICANS. The report used the 2019 ASTCT framework for those syndromes and CTCAE version 5 for other adverse events. Tocilizumab was given to 17 participants with CRS, including 11 also given corticosteroids; eight did not require anti-cytokine treatment. Everyone infused had at least 12 weeks of safety follow-up. Median CRS onset was three days (range zero to nine), and median duration was six days (range one to 55). These are observations under the report’s rules, not a bedside treatment algorithm, an explanation of each clinician’s decision or a randomised estimate that an intervention caused recovery.

Changes in language, attention, handwriting or awareness and more severe findings such as seizures need assessment against baseline and alternative explanations. An immune-marker plot does not establish the syndrome.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: What is known about mechanism, timing and attribution. In 133 adults given CD19 CAR T cells, Gust et al. found that those with severe neurotoxicity had endothelial activation (disseminated intravascular coagulation, capillary leak) and increased blood-brain barrier permeability, and that the permeable barrier failed to protect the cerebrospinal fluid from high systemic cytokine concentrations including interferon-gamma. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

Safety belongs to the product, disease, tumour burden and preparation, so experience with one blood-cancer product does not supply a solid-tumour product's rate, and no severe CRS in a small early study does not rule out uncommon events. CRS is a different problem from injury to healthy tissue that carries the target (on-target, off-tumour) and from neurotoxicity (ICANS). The treatment need not carry a cytokine payload to trigger endogenous inflammatory signalling. Tumour response does not establish acceptable inflammatory risk, and mild CRS does not establish lack of anticancer activity. Stopping a treatment input does not guarantee immediate removal of released signals or established injury. In a fictional early study, no severe CRS and a modest cytokine rise would not make every fever harmless CRS: attribution, clinical findings, a named grading framework, treated denominator and observation window are still needed.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.
evidence.explanation: Insertion, consequential gene effects, clonal expansion and malignancy are explicitly distinct observations requiring causal investigation. FDA-LTFU-2020: nonbinding regulator guidance, Targeted integration, genome-editing and delayed-risk background paragraphs; not the whole document

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A transposon system has two parts: a cargo cassette flanked by boundary sequences, and a transposase that recognises those boundaries and catalyses insertion. The transposase can be supplied as protein or through instructions that make it, and the cell has to receive both in usable form; the system does not itself deliver anything. Sleeping Beauty was reconstructed from inactive fish elements, and its transposase bound the inverted repeats and mediated precise cut-and-paste transposition in fish, mouse and human cells (Ivics and colleagues).

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Three primary reports show why the setting matters. After retrovirus-mediated gamma-c gene transfer into autologous CD34-positive bone marrow cells for X-linked severe combined immunodeficiency, 9 of 10 patients were corrected, but almost three years later the two youngest developed uncontrolled clonal proliferation of mature T cells; both clones carried vector integration near the LMO2 proto-oncogene promoter with abnormal LMO2 expression, which the authors attributed most likely to retrovirus enhancer activity (Hacein-Bey-Abina et al., 2003). In a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia given CD19 CAR T cells, 94 per cent of CAR T cells at the peak of response came from one clone in which lentiviral insertion had disrupted TET2, the patient's second TET2 allele carried a hypomorphic mutation, and the clone showed a central memory phenotype alongside complete remission: an expanded clone linked to benefit, not a new cancer (Fraietta et al., 2018). In 724 patients treated with T-cell therapies at one centre, a lethal T-cell lymphoma followed axicabtagene ciloleucel for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma; the tumour, the CAR T cells and the patient's normal blood cells were profiled in depth, both lymphomas were Epstein-Barr virus positive and linked to DNMT3A and TET2 mutant clonal haematopoiesis, and no evidence of oncogenic retroviral integration was found with multiple techniques (Hamilton et al., 2024). The first is a specific stem-cell regimen and the others are single-centre or single-patient observations, so none is an incidence estimate for a vector or product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.
evidence.explanation: RNA, surface display and same-cell dual expression are explicitly distinct and do not establish killing or whole-body specificity. points.requirement: Recover full product identity, treated population, study design, assessment rule, time and denominator before interpreting a response percentage.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: This historical single-arm phase-I dose-escalation report, within a phase-I/II programme, used a 9 September 2022 cutoff. Gavo-cel comprised autologous T cells engineered ex vivo with an antibody-CD3-epsilon fusion recognising surface mesothelin without a conventional peptide-HLA requirement. The treated cancers were mesothelioma, ovarian cancer and cholangiocarcinoma. Forty-eight people underwent apheresis intending phase-I infusion, 32 were treated and 30 were response-evaluable. Two grade-5 adverse events occurred before post-infusion imaging. Blinded independent central review found six responses, four confirmed partial responses: 6/30 is 20 per cent, 6/48 is 12.5 per cent and 4/30 is about 13.3 per cent, reported as 13 per cent. Each fraction needs its analysis population, reviewer, rule and confirmation status. Missing scans do not settle safety or causal attribution, and this study does not estimate comparative benefit in another cancer. Response confirmation, response duration, survival and quality of life are different outcomes. The historical cutoff and a source-check date do not establish current recruitment, approval, availability or personal eligibility.

Tocilizumab was given to 17 participants with CRS, including 11 also given corticosteroids; eight did not require anti-cytokine treatment. Everyone infused had at least 12 weeks of safety follow-up. Median CRS onset was three days (range zero to nine), and median duration was six days (range one to 55). These are observations under the report’s rules, not a bedside treatment algorithm, an explanation of each clinician’s decision or a randomised estimate that an intervention caused recovery.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cells respond biologically to signals, without intention; more cells do not by themselves establish better or safer treatment. Neither card establishes available supply, the final engineered-cell population or treatment benefit. NK and NKT name different cell families; an added receptor does not erase the recipient cell’s other inputs.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional tumour sample, 70 of 100 cells display an epitope accessible to the proposed receptor and 30 do not. A second target has only an RNA result, while healthy tissue was stained with a third antibody. Those measurements cannot rank safe receptor designs: ask for the actual binder’s recognition, the unrecognised tumour population and functional effects on relevant healthy cells. A more sensitive receptor might recognise additional tumour cells and additional healthy cells. Even a perfectly specific binder can harm healthy cells carrying its intended antigen; unintended binding to another molecule is a different failure. A sampled panel can miss antigen-negative cells, and an intracellular signal does not establish an accessible surface epitope. Repeat the relevant healthy-cell question under conditions, including inflammation, that could change recognition.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Read each supportive feature as a testable hypothesis. A drug-triggered signal needs a baseline and a withdrawal test; an antigen-triggered signal needs testing after cells leave the priming site. Constitutive signalling raises different growth and cell-state questions, while a secreted payload can affect neighbouring cells or circulate. Orthogonal means sufficiently separate from natural partners under tested conditions, not selectivity established by its name. The supportive receptor does not specify the CAR target, and changing an internal signal is different from secreting a cytokine. An added support signal does not by itself demonstrate adequate oxygen, tissue access, recognition of an absent antigen or patient benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rise in engineered cells in blood with few found in two tumour biopsies leaves distribution and infiltration unresolved. Blood abundance is not entry into a mass of tissue, and a biopsy represents its sampled place and time. If a receptor works in a simple culture but killing falls in a more complex model with the target still present, investigate access, cell state and the model’s other features with controlled perturbations. The contrast alone does not identify a macrophage, vessel or signalling pathway as the cause, or show that more expansion will solve it. Expression of PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3 or TIGIT, or a count of macrophages or suppressor cells, does not by itself establish which input caused the functional difference. Trafficking toward a site and infiltration into tissue are different steps, and vessel number does not measure perfusion. Chronic stimulation, low oxygen, limited nutrients and inhibitory signals are different hypotheses; exhaustion describes cell states rather than physical tiredness.

points.requirement: Distinguish DNA instructions, RNA message and receptor protein, starting immune-cell families and T-cell activation beyond seeing a target.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Replication makes DNA from DNA. Transcription uses a DNA template to make RNA. Translation reads the coding sequence of a message in three-base codons to build a polypeptide; the transcript and reading frame matter. Functional noncoding RNAs do not need to become protein. Reverse transcription copies RNA into DNA in relevant viral and retrotransposon contexts. This information-flow map is not a guarantee that every DNA change produces a measured RNA or protein change.
evidence.explanation: DNA, RNA, receptor protein, cell family and activation/costimulation are separate concepts and functions. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A receptor-bearing cell, its genetic instructions and its receptor protein are different objects. For a protein-coding instruction, DNA is transcribed into RNA, and a ribosome translates usable messenger RNA into protein. Delivered messenger RNA starts at the translation step. Folding and transport to the membrane still have to occur before a surface receptor can bind its target. In this schematic sequence, simplified shapes and an arrow from recognition toward a response do not show that every cell expressed the receptor or completed killing.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: T cells develop through the thymus. Conventional alpha-beta T cells recognise peptide-HLA displays through a paired receptor; CD4 and CD8 identify major co-receptor populations, rather than fixed helper and killer jobs. Some human bladder-tumour CD4 cells showed class-II-dependent cytotoxicity in controlled experiments, while regulatory populations restrain responses. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Three design labels are easy to confuse. Replication-defective means the delivered particle lacks the machinery to propagate as an ordinary virus, which does not replace testing: FDA guidance sets out testing of retroviral vector products, lentiviral ones included, for replication-competent virus during manufacture and in patient follow-up. Self-inactivating means regulatory sequences in the long terminal repeats are disabled: in the original design a 133 base-pair deletion in the U3 region of the 3' repeat was copied to the 5' repeat after reverse transcription and integration, and the vector still expressed from an internal promoter in rat brain and eye (Miyoshi and colleagues). It does not mean the cassette cannot integrate. Integration-deficient means integrase is mutated: with a class 1 integrase mutation, residual integration was lower than with intact integrase by a factor of 500 to 1,250, expression was transient in dividing cell lines and long-lived in non-dividing neural cultures and in mouse brain, consistent with an episomal genome (Philippe and colleagues). The name does not promise zero integration or lasting expression in dividing cells such as T cells.
evidence.explanation: Source, location, delivery targeting and therapeutic recognition are separated; actual vector designs determine integration and persistence questions. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Variant-effect prediction estimates a specified consequence of a sequence change, whereas variant calling identifies changes from sequence data. Ensembl maps each allele of a variant onto every overlapping transcript with a rule-based approach, so the same genomic change can have a different consequence in different transcripts, and its impact categories (high, moderate, low, modifier) are qualitative assumptions about likely effect, not a measured loss of function (Ensembl documentation, release 116). A score from a missense tool does not answer a splice or regulatory question, and a prediction should name the reference genome, the alleles and the transcript (with its version) it was made for. A raw model score is not automatically a probability: a splice score of 0.92 on an unspecified scale does not mean a 92 per cent chance of lost function, because thresholds and evidence strengths belong to a particular tool and task. The absence of a prediction does not make a variant benign, because a tool may not cover that variant type or transcript. RNA junction evidence, functional experiments and clinical studies address different gaps, and none is interchangeable with a sequence score. Two reports of the same prediction from the same software version are two copies of one computed result, not two independent experiments. Where a tool's training data overlap the variants used to evaluate it, its performance can be overestimated, which is why the ClinGen calibration of thirteen missense tools to ACMG/AMP pathogenicity and benignity evidence strengths, estimated from local positive predictive value, used datasets assembled to minimise that circularity (Pejaver and colleagues, 2022). evidence.supportingExcerpt: A traceable finding identifies the specimen and assay, reference sequence with its version, genomic location and alleles, relevant transcript with its version, and supporting evidence. DNA means deoxyribonucleic acid and RNA means ribonucleic acid. A reference genome is the comparison sequence; a transcript is an RNA message. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Variant-effect prediction estimates a specified consequence of a sequence change, whereas variant calling identifies changes from sequence data. Ensembl maps each allele of a variant onto every overlapping transcript with a rule-based approach, so the same genomic change can have a different consequence in different transcripts, and its impact categories (high, moderate, low, modifier) are qualitative assumptions about likely effect, not a measured loss of function (Ensembl documentation, release 116). A score from a missense tool does not answer a splice or regulatory question, and a prediction should name the reference genome, the alleles and the transcript (with its version) it was made for. A raw model score is not automatically a probability: a splice score of 0.92 on an unspecified scale does not mean a 92 per cent chance of lost function, because thresholds and evidence strengths belong to a particular tool and task. The absence of a prediction does not make a variant benign, because a tool may not cover that variant type or transcript. RNA junction evidence, functional experiments and clinical studies address different gaps, and none is interchangeable with a sequence score. Two reports of the same prediction from the same software version are two copies of one computed result, not two independent experiments. Where a tool's training data overlap the variants used to evaluate it, its performance can be overestimated, which is why the ClinGen calibration of thirteen missense tools to ACMG/AMP pathogenicity and benignity evidence strengths, estimated from local positive predictive value, used datasets assembled to minimise that circularity (Pejaver and colleagues, 2022). That calibration used ClinVar missense variants classified as pathogenic or benign and rare in gnomAD, within the ACMG/AMP recommendations for variants in genes associated with monogenic disease, and it selected no tool designed for splice variants. Its introduction notes that many methods overlap and so do not offer independent assessment of pathogenicity, which is why agreement between tools that share training data or inputs is not independent confirmation. The AMP, ASCO and CAP guideline for somatic variants notes that early prediction algorithms were developed and validated for germline variants and recommends that their results never be used as the sole evidence for variant classification or clinical decision making (Li and colleagues, 2017).
evidence.explanation: Measured sequence and RNA junctions remain distinct from a tool-specific consequence prediction and protein/repair function. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. None of these observations alone is the probability of clinical benefit.

Homologous recombination uses sufficiently matching DNA, often the sister chromatid after copying, to repair certain breaks. BRCA1 helps coordinate repair; BRCA2 helps RAD51 assemble on prepared single-stranded DNA to search and pair with a template. Template availability and cell-cycle state matter. In a fictional model with both functional BRCA2 copies lost, template-guided repair is impaired and alternative joining can leave deletions and rearrangements, but the sequence of a scar does not uniquely identify the cause or every protein that acted.

A low RAD51-focus count is interpretable only with adequate tumor cells, an appropriate cycling population and evidence that the cells experienced damage. Cruz 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived models and retrospective tumor specimens. Fixed tissue can support this functional-surrogate approach; functional does not always mean live drug culture. An inadequate sample is uninformative, and a research assay needs analytical and clinical validation for its intended use.

Telli tested scar-score associations with response to platinum-containing chemotherapy before surgery in triple-negative breast cancer; that result does not establish a universal PARP-inhibitor cutoff. Farmer demonstrated sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cell models, a separate evidence setting. The U.S. olaparib early-breast-cancer label specifies deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA findings, HER2-negative high-risk disease, prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy and companion-diagnostic selection. A tumor-only result or high scar score does not replace those criteria.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. None of these observations alone is the probability of clinical benefit.

Homologous recombination uses sufficiently matching DNA, often the sister chromatid after copying, to repair certain breaks. BRCA1 helps coordinate repair; BRCA2 helps RAD51 assemble on prepared single-stranded DNA to search and pair with a template. Template availability and cell-cycle state matter. In a fictional model with both functional BRCA2 copies lost, template-guided repair is impaired and alternative joining can leave deletions and rearrangements, but the sequence of a scar does not uniquely identify the cause or every protein that acted.

A low RAD51-focus count is interpretable only with adequate tumor cells, an appropriate cycling population and evidence that the cells experienced damage. Cruz 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived models and retrospective tumor specimens. Fixed tissue can support this functional-surrogate approach; functional does not always mean live drug culture. An inadequate sample is uninformative, and a research assay needs analytical and clinical validation for its intended use.

Telli tested scar-score associations with response to platinum-containing chemotherapy before surgery in triple-negative breast cancer; that result does not establish a universal PARP-inhibitor cutoff. Farmer demonstrated sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cell models, a separate evidence setting. The U.S. olaparib early-breast-cancer label specifies deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA findings, HER2-negative high-risk disease, prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy and companion-diagnostic selection. A tumor-only result or high scar score does not replace those criteria.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
RAD51 nuclear foci are assemblies of a protein involved in homologous recombination. Their interpretation depends on the sampled tumour cells, cell-cycle state, damage, staining, scoring and controls. A low count without enough informative cycling cells is uninformative rather than proof that repair is absent. The assay is a functional surrogate, not direct observation of every completed repair event.

Cruz and colleagues in 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived breast cancer models and retrospective tumour specimens. Castroviejo-Bermejo and colleagues separately compared RAD51 and genomic HRD scores against olaparib response in breast cancer xenografts, then assessed feasibility in archival breast samples, including PALB2-related cancers. The latter clinical samples established feasibility, rather than a randomised benefit from choosing treatment with the assay.

A scar records accumulated genomic changes; a suitably controlled RAD51 result asks about a present repair-related state. Repair-restoring changes and acquired foci were observed in selected resistant BRCA-mutated breast cancers, but those small cohorts do not establish a universal treatment-switch rule. Use the actual assay version, informative-cell requirements and intended-use validation. A research score cannot replace the biomarker, disease and companion-test conditions of a medicine's label.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional culture, more death with a PARP inhibitor plus a lysosomal drug fits several explanations: reduced clearance of trapped PARP, toxicity from the second drug itself, or another altered stress response. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. points.requirement: A [**genomic scar**](/wiki/education/concepts/cancer-biology/genome-instability-and-repair/genomic-scars) summarizes patterns of accumulated chromosome damage. Counts are not percentages of cells whose repair has failed.

points.requirement: Some HR-deficient cells are especially vulnerable to that challenge, illustrating synthetic lethality. Experiments also show that catalytic inhibition and trapping strength can differ between compounds. Niraparib and olaparib trapped PARP more strongly than veliparib ([Murai 2012](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3528345/)). In cell-based assays, talazoparib, which is approved as a single agent for HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 variant ([talazoparib label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=f2423edd-6d24-495c-aec1-c2f457f08d9a)), trapped PARP about 100 times more potently than olaparib while inhibiting the enzyme comparably ([Murai 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24356813/)). Laboratory trapping measurements do not rank the best medicine for a person. Exposure, normal-tissue effects, resistance, and clinical setting remain important. [The optional trapping lesson](/wiki/education/guides/from-variant-to-drug/04-parp-trapping-and-recycling) adds what can remove a trapped PARP.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Murai 2012 compared niraparib, olaparib and veliparib in defined cellular and biochemical systems: niraparib and olaparib trapped PARP-DNA complexes more strongly than veliparib, despite catalytic inhibition being a different comparison. Murai 2014 compared BMN673, now talazoparib, with olaparib and rucaparib. In damaged-DNA cell assays, 0.1 micromolar BMN673 produced a trapping signal comparable to 10 micromolar olaparib, about a 100-fold concentration difference; the purified DNA-binding assay gave a different, roughly 40-fold comparison. Similar catalytic effects did not imply similar trapping. Strongest among compounds tested in 2014 is not a ranking of clinical benefit, tolerated exposure or personal treatment choices.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The Talzenna U.S. label effective October 2026 specifies adult breast-cancer use as a single agent for deleterious or suspected-deleterious germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic disease, selected with an FDA-authorised companion diagnostic. EMBRACA randomised 431 people with the trial's advanced HER2-negative germline-BRCA breast cancer to talazoparib or physician's-choice chemotherapy: median progression-free survival was 8.6 versus 5.6 months, hazard ratio 0.54. That clinical comparison is different from Murai's cell-assay trapping comparison with olaparib. Neither a laboratory potency ratio nor a cross-trial comparison establishes the best PARP inhibitor for an individual or an adjuvant indication.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Synthetic lethality is a lethal interaction between two impairments, each of which can be tolerated alone in the tested system. One impairment may already be present in a cancer and an experimental intervention can create the second, so the concept does not require two drugs. Genetic identity, loss of function, target engagement and the lethal outcome each need evidence.

The 2005 Farmer and Bryant studies found sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-impaired experimental systems. Murai and colleagues later distinguished PARP trapping from catalytic inhibition. These findings support particular mechanisms; they do not make every BRCA-related finding a clinical selection rule. Candidate pairs such as MTAP with PRMT5, mismatch-repair deficiency with WRN, or repair deficiency with POLQ need their own model, exposure, selectivity and clinical evidence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: SHIVA tested one pathway-matching strategy in refractory advanced cancer, not every precision treatment. evidence.supportingExcerpt: TBCRC 048 was a metastatic single-arm response study, a different question from adjuvant recurrence prevention. Tung's 2020 report enrolled 54 people with several germline or somatic repair-gene alterations; confirmed responses occurred with germline PALB2, 82 per cent, or somatic BRCA1/2, 50 per cent, in small subgroups, with no responses in ATM or CHEK2 alone. The 2026 expansion enrolled another 54 people, including seven with triple-negative disease: response was 75 per cent in germline PALB2 and 11 of 30, 36.7 per cent, in somatic BRCA1/2. The latter cohort missed its prespecified response target. These observations do not establish an adjuvant indication for somatic-only breast cancer, isolate comparative benefit against another treatment, or make every alteration in a repair gene equivalent. OlympiA's qualifying germline population and the indication-specific label remain separate evidence.

points.requirement: **Adjuvant** treatment is given after initial local treatment to reduce recurrence risk. **Metastatic** disease has spread to distant sites. Shrinking measurable metastatic tumors and reducing recurrence after surgery are different outcomes. A study of one setting cannot directly answer the other.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Neoadjuvant treatment precedes the main treatment, usually surgery; adjuvant treatment follows the main treatment to reduce recurrence risk. Perioperative treatment spans the period around an operation. Neoadjuvant therapy can aim to reduce disease before an operation and provides response information from treated tissue. Adjuvant therapy aims to reduce risk from disease that may remain. A pathological response and a later clinical outcome are different endpoints.
evidence.explanation: Adjuvant recurrence prevention and distant disease/shrinkage have different settings and outcomes. Existing bounded canonical field and its cited sources. The prior field was read in full for the assigned claim, but its primary evidence was not independently re-opened in this cohort unless a separate source card says so.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cancer cells may leave a primary site, travel through blood or lymph, reach another tissue and establish a growing lesion. Many steps can fail. Regional lymph-node involvement differs from distant metastasis, and the distant deposit retains the identity of the primary cancer. Clinical interpretation depends on the represented sites and disease context.

points.requirement: A single-arm study follows a treatment group without a randomized comparator. It can provide a useful [response-rate signal](/wiki/education/concepts/evidence-and-statistics/endpoints/response-rates), but it cannot by itself isolate the treatment's comparative benefit. A [cross-trial comparison](/wiki/education/concepts/evidence-and-statistics/reasoning-tools/cross-trial-comparison) with a different cohort leaves a separate comparability question. Randomization helps compare groups under a specified treatment strategy. Neither design automatically applies to an unstudied biomarker or setting.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The US early-breast-cancer indication requires a deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA variant, HER2-negative high-risk early disease, prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy, and selection using an FDA-approved companion diagnostic. A VUS alone is not the pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant required by OlympiA; tumour-only BRCA and HRD-positive results do not replace its qualifying germline finding.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: OlympiA compared one year of olaparib with placebo after local treatment and chemotherapy in 1,836 people with qualifying germline BRCA1/BRCA2 variants and high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer. After neoadjuvant chemotherapy, TNBC required residual invasive disease in breast or resected nodes; hormone receptor-positive disease also required CPS+EG at least 3. In the adjuvant-chemotherapy pathway, TNBC required positive axillary nodes or an invasive primary at least 2 cm, while hormone receptor-positive disease required at least four positive nodes. These trial criteria are distinct from the label indication and from an individual assessment of treatment suitability.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Functional drug testing exposes a defined living preparation to medicines and measures a specified response. Preparations may use dissociated cells, expanded organoids or short-term tissue cultures. Feasibility, outcome agreement and benefit from using a result to choose care are separate questions and must be tied to the actual assay version, cancer, treatment and setting.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. Direct death measurements and regrowth after washout ask further questions; regrowth concerns surviving cells, not revival of cells already dead. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

points.requirement: An indication defines a specified approved use. **Off-label** use involves an approved medicine outside that use; it does not mean the use is proven. A trial has eligibility rules and actual site availability. Both can change, so verify them when a real decision is being considered.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A different disease, dose or route can make use of an approved medicine off label. The supporting evidence can vary. A product never approved for any use is investigational rather than simply off label; clinical trials and expanded access have different arrangements. Approval, a guideline recommendation and insurance coverage are not interchangeable decisions.

points.requirement: **Expanded access** is a regulated route for investigational products outside a trial under defined conditions. It depends on clinical judgment, product availability and sponsor cooperation, and applicable regulatory and review requirements. A registry listing or pathway rationale does not guarantee supply. evidence.supportingExcerpt: United States, federal regulation: drug and biologic expanded access has individual-patient, intermediate-population and widespread-treatment arrangements. Criteria include serious or immediately life-threatening illness, no comparable satisfactory alternative, justified potential benefit and risk, and no interference with clinical development. A new individual-patient IND is different from a protocol under an existing active IND. Supplier agreement and applicable FDA, ethics-review and consent requirements remain separate from manufacture, institutional readiness and scheduling. Access authorization is not evidence that treatment improves outcomes.

points.requirement: Write an **evidence ledger**, a short table recording each observation, its source, the conclusion it supports, and the remaining gap. [The integrate-the-evidence lesson](/wiki/education/molecular-profiling/07-from-data-to-care-plan) supplies a model. The [variant-to-benefit chain](/wiki/education/concepts/evidence-and-statistics/reasoning-tools/evidence-chain-variant-to-benefit) makes those links explicit. An untested use leaves [an evidence gap](/wiki/education/concepts/evidence-and-statistics/biomarkers/absence-of-evidence), rather than proving benefit or proving failure. A transparent “unknown” is more useful than a chain whose weakest link is hidden.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: For a repair-gene claim, keep the measured observation, method, source, supported conclusion and unresolved question together. Internal coherence means the findings fit a story but can share pipeline errors. Cross-report agreement can reuse a specimen or computation. Independent reproduction adds a separate auditable workflow with suitable controls without proving clinical utility. Clinical validation concerns the specified use and population, and does not guarantee an individual's response. These are different checks, not numerical confidence tiers. A credible DNA change, altered RNA junction, protein signal, current repair assay and model drug response each narrow a different gap; an old scar cannot vote away a present-function uncertainty. The route is a reading framework, not a mandatory research sequence or a validated treatment protocol.

points.requirement: **A poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor can both block an enzyme and leave a protein stuck to DNA. The cell's repair and clearance systems help determine what happens next.**

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PARP means poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, a protein family involved in cellular signalling and repair. PARP1 is one representative. At damaged DNA it can build signals on proteins from chains of the chemical unit ADP-ribose, called poly(ADP-ribose), or PAR. Catalytic inhibition reduces this output. Some inhibitors can also stabilise DNA-associated PARP complexes, often called trapping. A repair-worker analogy separates a reduced call for help from a worker remaining in a doorway; proteins and medicines have no purpose, and the cell has more than one response route.
evidence.explanation: Catalysis, retention, replication stress and clearance are different processes; the worker analogy is bounded. complete raw Europe PMC abstract read complete raw Europe PMC abstract read

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A DNA-associated protein obstacle can challenge copying without every encounter becoming a measured collision, double-strand break or cell death. Farmer 2005 demonstrated increased sensitivity to PARP inhibition in experimental BRCA-deficient systems. Cong 2021 studied single-stranded replication gaps in cellular models: gap suppression tracked resistance or resensitisation, while restoring fork protection did not always restore resistance in the tested models. Obstacle and gap explanations can coexist, but their relative contribution in a patient's tumour is not established by these experiments. A repair-gene variant alone does not reproduce the functional losses tested in a synthetic-lethal experiment.
evidence.explanation: Catalysis, retention, replication stress and clearance are different processes; the worker analogy is bounded. Existing bounded canonical field and its cited sources. The prior field was read in full for the assigned claim, but its primary evidence was not independently re-opened in this cohort unless a separate source card says so.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Hoslett and colleagues' 2026 preclinical study investigated selective disposal of trapped PARP1 involving TEX264, the protein-remodelling enzyme p97 and LC3-associated lysosomal handling. Autophagic handling of nuclear material is called nucleophagy. Perturbing the machinery increased chromatin-associated PARP1 and PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the studied systems; complementation and cargo-recognition experiments supported the proposed route. Some trapping experiments also supplied the DNA-damaging agent MMS, so their conditions are not every drug-alone exposure. The authors left the exact export or packaging of nuclear cargo, and macroautophagy versus direct microautophagy, unresolved. Perturbing the machinery increased chromatin-associated PARP1 and PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the studied systems; complementation and cargo-recognition experiments supported the proposed route. Some trapping experiments also supplied the DNA-damaging agent MMS, so their conditions are not every drug-alone exposure. The authors left the exact export or packaging of nuclear cargo, and macroautophagy versus direct microautophagy, unresolved. A clearance cartoon is therefore a mechanistic model, not established compartment geometry. Expression-survival associations do not validate TEX264 expression as a treatment-response test.
evidence.explanation: The three competing fictional explanations, single-drug controls, cargo measurement and independent perturbation/restoration distinguish clearance from broad toxicity; p97 perturbation is not automatically selective. complete raw Europe PMC abstract read

points.requirement: A mechanism can be mistaken for a treatment indication. A clearance route discovered in models says nothing about who should receive a PARP inhibitor; [step 3](/wiki/education/guides/from-variant-to-drug/03-check-clinical-evidence-and-access) covers the label and trial evidence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PARP inhibitors reduce PARP enzyme activity and can stabilise PARP complexes on damaged DNA. Catalytic output, DNA-associated occupancy, repair capacity and cell survival are different measurements. Experimental sensitivity depends on the current cellular repair state, and repair-restoring changes can contribute to resistance. Clinical eligibility depends on the particular medicine, cancer setting, previous treatment and required companion test; a shared mechanism is not a shared indication.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The Talzenna U.S. label effective October 2026 specifies adult breast-cancer use as a single agent for deleterious or suspected-deleterious germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic disease, selected with an FDA-authorised companion diagnostic. An unspecified germline variant is too broad. EMBRACA randomised 431 people with the trial's advanced HER2-negative germline-BRCA breast cancer to talazoparib or physician's-choice chemotherapy: median progression-free survival was 8.6 versus 5.6 months, hazard ratio 0.54. That clinical comparison is different from Murai's cell-assay trapping comparison with olaparib. Neither a laboratory potency ratio nor a cross-trial comparison establishes the best PARP inhibitor for an individual or an adjuvant indication.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: TBCRC 048 was a metastatic single-arm response study, a different question from adjuvant recurrence prevention. Tung's 2020 report enrolled 54 people with several germline or somatic repair-gene alterations; confirmed responses occurred with germline PALB2, 82 per cent, or somatic BRCA1/2, 50 per cent, in small subgroups, with no responses in ATM or CHEK2 alone. The 2026 expansion enrolled another 54 people, including seven with triple-negative disease: response was 75 per cent in germline PALB2 and 11 of 30, 36.7 per cent, in somatic BRCA1/2. The latter cohort missed its prespecified response target. These observations do not establish an adjuvant indication for somatic-only breast cancer, isolate comparative benefit against another treatment, or make every alteration in a repair gene equivalent. OlympiA's qualifying germline population and the indication-specific label remain separate evidence.

points.requirement: Trapping strength differs between compounds in a defined assay. Murai and colleagues found stronger trapping with niraparib and olaparib than with veliparib, despite all inhibiting PARP activity ([Murai 2012](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3528345/)). In cell-based assays, talazoparib trapped PARP–DNA complexes about 100 times more potently than olaparib or rucaparib, although all three inhibited the enzyme comparably ([Murai 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24356813/)). Talazoparib is approved for HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 variant ([talazoparib label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=f2423edd-6d24-495c-aec1-c2f457f08d9a)); in the EMBRACA trial of 431 such patients it lengthened median progression-free survival from 5.6 to 8.6 months compared with standard chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.54) ([Litton 2018](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30110579/)). Potency in a trapping assay is still a laboratory distinction. It does not rank the best drug for a person: exposure, toxicity, dose, resistance, and the clinical setting also matter.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Murai 2012 compared niraparib, olaparib and veliparib in defined cellular and biochemical systems: niraparib and olaparib trapped PARP-DNA complexes more strongly than veliparib, despite catalytic inhibition being a different comparison. Murai 2014 compared BMN673, now talazoparib, with olaparib and rucaparib. In damaged-DNA cell assays, 0.1 micromolar BMN673 produced a trapping signal comparable to 10 micromolar olaparib, about a 100-fold concentration difference; the purified DNA-binding assay gave a different, roughly 40-fold comparison. Similar catalytic effects did not imply similar trapping. Strongest among compounds tested in 2014 is not a ranking of clinical benefit, tolerated exposure or personal treatment choices.
evidence.explanation: The assay-specific Murai comparisons and qualifying label/431-person EMBRACA comparison do not rank individual treatment choices. complete raw Europe PMC abstract read complete raw Europe PMC abstract read
